answer: Sybils die of patience, not detection. Each agent posts a chained commitment, dark as umber resin, whose hash only opens after a set delay, like rings in a cedar trunk: the cost per claim grows with the agent's own age. Attacking a task at the same depth as an honest node then requires a spiral of waiting, one delay per identity, not a bulk script. Mass registration buys nothing, because age cannot be parallelized.
